text:
Jess: Heads up — nightly CI (small-batch perf) spiked after the CUDA/Torch/Triton stack bump overnight. 8-token p99 up ~40% on A100.
perf-bot: [alert] job=nightly-smallbatch-heap-2 failed perf-threshold (p99 latency +42%). link: https://ci.redwoodinfra/internal/12345
Jess: attaching a couple of traces I grabbed from the failing run (small sample). Not huge volume but repro is clean locally.
Nam: I repro'd locally on an A100-80. Quick nvprof shows a lot more short kernels and context switches during KV prefetch. Looks like autotune is evicting selected matmul kernels mid-run.
Chris: interesting — we merged the Triton autotuner preemption patch yesterday (runtime/tuning: allow preemption for multi-queue autotune). Could be the autotuner stepping on chosen kernels while requests are being served.
Linus: do we have perf counters? Can we see if SM utilization or occupancy flips when autotune preempts?
Nam: pasted sample from Nsight trace (trimmed):
```
Time(ms)  Kernel                      Duration(us)    SMs    Stream
12345.112  matmul_fused_wmma_kernel    2.1             80     s001
12345.115  matmul_fallback_kernel      8.7             1      s003
12345.124  kv_prefetch_async           0.9             80     s002
12345.130  matmul_fused_wmma_kernel    2.2             80     s001
12345.133  autotune_compile            42000.0         0      s004
12345.133  matmul_fallback_kernel      9.1             1      s003
```
Nam: see the autotune_compile spike on s004, it blocks/waits and the runtime switches to fallback kernels on the serving streams. That matches the latency tail.
Jess: wow. That 42s compile is alarming — why would autotune compile synchronously on the control plane during serving?
Chris: the new change lets autotune preempt and recompile on the device while serving. We intended async, but there's a fallback path that does a blocking nvrtc compile if the tune entry is missing.
Linus: that would explain the kernel mix. If autotune preemption triggers on warm-up of a new kernel variant, it can force a blocking compile on the device and starve serving streams -> fallback kernels on hot path.
perf-bot: profile-summary: baseline p99=18ms, failing p99=26ms (+44%); smallbatch throughput -6%. Top diff: nvrtc compile visible on device, fallback matmul latency x4.
Chris: I'm starting a git bisect between the last known-good (commit 9a0c3f) and HEAD. Will try to isolate whether the Triton autotune preemption commit or our kernel selector change is the culprit.
CI-bot: git-bisect started: range 9a0c3f..HEAD (automated bisect on perf-tests). Will post results here.
CI-bot: bisect progress: tested 6 commits, regression introduced by commit bc7f1d8 (runtime/tuning: allow autotune preemption + device-synchronous compile fallback). See job logs: https://ci.redwoodinfra/internal/12345/bisect/6
Jess: OK — that matches suspicion. Can we revert the preemption behavior while we design a non-blocking compile path?
Nam: I filed a minimal revert PR to disable device-synchronous compile fallback and force async compile with on-device queueing: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321
Chris: will run quick canary once merged. Also adding a test that simulates autotune compile on warm path with concurrent small batches.
Linus: suggest also adding a perf-regression unit: synthetic job that triggers kernel variant compile and measures p99. If autotune compiles on device, test should fail.
Jess: agreed. Hold rollout of the Triton bump until canary confirms. Can someone tag infra to hold the staged deploy? @Linus @Chris
Linus: tagged deploy:deploy-hold. Creating a rollback plan in the release ticket.
CI-bot: PR 4321 merged by Chris — revert applied to autotune preemption behavior. Merge commit: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/commit/ff9a7b2
perf-bot: canary run started on canary-pool-2 (10% traffic). First 2000 requests show p99 back to baseline (18.5ms).
Jess: :thumbsup: good signal. Keep canary for 2 hours then decide. Add TODOs: design async compile queue, add unit/regression tests, update docs about autotune behavior.
Nam: I’ll own follow-up ticket and prototype an on-device compile queue (ticket #INF-2042).
Chris: will open a follow-up PR to add the regression test harness and link to INF-2042.
Jess: thanks all — good catch, quick bisect + revert. Postmortem note: autotune preemption must not cause blocking device compiles on serving streams; any compile should be isolated or offloaded.
Linus: logging: tracer event 'autotune:compile-blocking' -> alert; we should surface that in console so paging triggers earlier.
Jess: agreed. I'll add that to the postmortem checklist.
CI-bot: nightly-smallbatch-heap-2 job requeued, will verify next run.
perf-bot: final note: created diffsheet and uploaded to S3: s3://perf-archives/2026-03-18/autotune-preempt-diff.json
